T3 `wall` has it on an enceinte's trace, a stretch's anchor vertex and a gate's crossing among them. T4 `road` has it on a way's, a raised way's or a tunnel's chain. T9 `shape` has it on an island's key. T6 `place` has `instance` on a hood pin (add, move, remove, restyle). It has no shore or coast, enceinte-trace, stretch-anchor, tunnel-chain or island-key `moveVertex` pair. Its T6 row is '`instance` add (a hood pin)' and its T8 row '`instance` groups of trees' (plant, thin, restyle). issues.claim: `advance` on a dossier-bound document is refused, but no unit says what the call returns. §11.2 types `advance(h, req, opts?): Promise<ApplyResult>` with the comment 'refused on a dossier-bound document'. Its `ApplyResult` has only `ok`, `conflict` and `confirm` members, and no catalogue key is named for the refusal. V06 §2.3 calls it 'the dossier-clock case of the dossier-owned refusal', offering 'Make a what-if copy and advance it'. V09 §4.9 words it as `refuse.dossierClock`, codes '§11.2's `advance` refused on a dossier-bound document'. So a caller that does not pre-check — volume 10's harness running the clerk's `advance` (V09 §4.3's `advance` row: 'also from: the clerk's proposal'), or a script through §11.2 — gets an answer of undefined shape. The matrix lists `advance` (V06–V09, V06–V10, V09–V10) but not this refusal. That makes it an undefined edge of the embedding API (principle (11)).

It then reads 'an answer carrying a `bent` `MsgRef` … its alternatives `propose` actions — for a placement bend each of the preview's plots', and step 4 returns 'its bend line …, its counts, its fates counted by kind …, its effects'. issues.claim: File g item 121 (the resolution adjuster; J134), routed by canon.md's ruling 'File g items 121, 122 and 123 routed', names rendering's parts as §8.8, §8.4 (g), §12.1, §12.5 and §12.8. issues.required_change: Write item 121's rendering part at build depth as new design. §8.8: the Resolution ladder 3 · 2 · 1.5 · 1 · 0.75 · 0.5, the two steps below 1 new (tiles drawn below CSS density and scaled up). A manual level sets d = min(device pixel ratio, the level's height ÷ the screen's height in CSS px), rounded down to the ladder. The ultra tier has a 512 MB canvas ceiling and tile-DPR cap 3. The live view never draws more than the 4K pixel count (≈ 8.3 M device px); larger screens are scaled up, and exports are not bound by it. The live Auto loop: a frame-time p95 over the tier's frame budget through 2 s steps one rung down; a p95 under 60 % of the budget through 10 s, with the canvas need fitting, steps one rung up. A change is applied only when the view settles, at most once per 10 s, and a device-pixel-ratio change re-evaluates at once. A manual level the device cannot hold draws the nearest level that fits and says so. §8.4 (g): the order of what Auto gives up — lighting detail (full precision → the standard surface → the half-resolution global term), then sharpness (the tile DPR down to 1), then the light pass (the vector rung), then the steps below 1; labels, text, the chrome and every overlay always at the device pixel ratio. §12.1: calibration picks ultra only where the device reports its memory and the benchmark clears the tier's bar. §12.5: the frame budgets the loop holds and its settle rule. §12.8: memory per tier, ultra included. Exports are byte-identical whatever the display setting.
